biography.background: Roy Asberry Cooper III (born June 13, 1957). Six-time statewide winner with 38+ years in NC public office. Announced Senate bid July 28, 2025 for the seat vacated by retiring Sen. Thom Tillis. Faces no significant primary opposition. $12.3M cash on hand entering 2026; raised $7M in Q4 2025 — led opponent Whatley nearly 2:1.

statedPositions.quote: Executive Order 80 (2018): 40% GHG reduction by 2025; signed HB 951 (2021): 70% carbon reduction by 2030, carbon neutral by 2050; Executive Order 246 (2022): strengthened to 50% reduction by 2030
statedPositions.notes: First 'purple state' governor to sign emissions mandate into law. NCLCV grade: A (2018, 2019). LCV Action Fund endorsed for 2026 Senate.

statedPositions.quote: HB 951 does not ban fossil fuels; sets targets and requires utilities to plan clean transition. NC became #9 nationally in clean energy jobs
statedPositions.notes: Not a rapid-transition / fossil fuel ban position — moderate Pole A. Bipartisan bill.

statedPositions.quote: Vetoed SB 41 (permit-to-purchase repeal, 2023) — overridden. Vetoed HB 398 (pistol permit repeal, 2021) — sustained. Created statewide Office of Violence Prevention (2023)
statedPositions.notes: NRA opposed him consistently. Multiple gun safety vetoes.

statedPositions.quote: Signed Medicaid expansion (2023): covered 600,000+ NCians. 2026 campaign: defends ACA subsidies, Medicaid, Medicare
statedPositions.notes: ACA-protect/expand position. No explicit Medicare for All or public option endorsement found.

statedPositions.quote: Medicaid expansion, teacher pay raises, $15/hr state employee minimum wage. 2026 campaign: 'cutting help for the poor' / 'give tax breaks to billionaires'
statedPositions.notes: Consistent record of expanding safety net programs.

statedPositions.quote: Vetoed multiple budgets over broad corporate and income tax cuts. Called for freezing high-income tax cuts; wanted revenue for education
statedPositions.notes: Progressive direction but with notable pragmatic compromises: eventually signed 2021 budget beginning corporate income tax phaseout. Also offered $930M+ in targeted corporate incentives to 22 corporations.

statedPositions.quote: Vetoed $6B+ voucher expansion (HB 10, 2024) — overridden. 'Sending taxpayer dollars to private schools with no accountability'
statedPositions.notes: Clear pro-public school position. Conflict note: sent his own children to private school.

statedPositions.quote: Created TREC (Task Force for Racial Equity in Criminal Justice, 2020). Signed SB 300 reform bills: duty to intervene, early intervention, diversity recruitment
statedPositions.notes: Not a 'defund' or abolition position; reform-focused. Moderate Pole A (~3-4).

statedPositions.quote: Commuted 15 death row sentences (largest in NC history). Signed First Step Act reforms. As AG: supervised 27 executions; said death penalty 'appropriate in certain heinous cases'
statedPositions.notes: Reform direction, not abolitionist. Complex record spanning AG and Governor tenures.

statedPositions.quote: Vetoed 3+ ICE cooperation bills. Signed DACA support letter with 10 governors
statedPositions.notes: Lean Pole A with some moderation. Nuance: signed one bill FLOC-AFL-CIO called 'anti-immigrant, anti-worker.'
Limited housing record. No strong record on zoning reform.
Planned Parenthood Action Fund and Reproductive Freedom for All endorsed for 2026. Strong pro-choice position.

votingRecord.notes: No congressional voting record, but extensive executive record as Governor (2017-2025) including vetoes, executive orders, and bill signings. Also served in NC legislature 1987-2001 but those votes are historical and less relevant to current positioning.

scorecards.notes: Grade A in 2018, 2019. LCV Action Fund endorsed for 2026 Senate.
NRA opposed him consistently. Multiple gun safety vetoes.

endorsements.notes: Called his entry a 'major coup for Senate Democrats.'

positionConflicts.conflict: Opposed broad corporate tax cuts but offered $930M+ in targeted incentives to 22 corporations
positionConflicts.resolution: Pragmatic moderation — opposes across-the-board cuts but uses targeted incentives for economic development

positionConflicts.conflict: Vetoed vouchers but sent his own kids to private school
positionConflicts.resolution: Personal choice vs. policy position — common for politicians. Policy position is clearly anti-voucher.

positionConflicts.conflict: Commuted 15 death row sentences as Governor but supervised 27 executions as AG and said death penalty 'appropriate in certain heinous cases'
positionConflicts.resolution: Evolution over time — moved from enforcement to clemency across career arc

positionConflicts.conflict: HB2 compromise repeal (2017) criticized by LGBTQ advocates as insufficient
positionConflicts.resolution: Pragmatic compromise under Republican supermajority legislature

evidenceSummary.notes: Roy Cooper has an extensive executive record as a two-term Governor providing high-confidence evidence on most axes. His gubernatorial vetoes, executive orders, and bill signings create a rich evidence base. Immigration is the axis with the most nuance — he vetoed ICE cooperation bills but signed one bill labor advocates criticized. Housing and transport have the least evidence. His positions are consistently center-left, moderate Democratic — not progressive/left wing. He is not a Medicare for All, Green New Deal, or defund-the-police candidate.
